title: Jio IPO Likely by October-End at $143-146 Billion Valuation
excerpt: Banking sources say Jio Platforms' estimated $3.8 billion public offering — potentially India's largest IPO — could list by month-end, with an anchor round before Dussehra and final SEBI filings in the week starting October 12.
body:
• Jio Platforms is likely to list by the end of October at an enterprise valuation of $143-146 billion, or above Rs 12 trillion, banking sources told PTI — the estimated $3.8 billion issue would be India's largest-ever public offer.
  • The company has completed overseas roadshows in the US, UK, Dubai, Hong Kong and Singapore, led by Akash Ambani and Isha Ambani, and is expected to file final papers with SEBI in the week starting October 12.
  • Investors watching the issue: the anchor round is expected before Dussehra, with the public offer opening post-Dussehra and before October 23; the draft prospectus proposes up to 27 crore fresh shares — about 2.9% of post-issue equity, small enough to signal a valuation-setting listing rather than a capital-raising one.
  • Reliance Industries holds about 66.4% of Jio Platforms while Meta and Google together own roughly 17.7%; the offering would be the Reliance group's first IPO since 2008.

India's biggest-ever public offering is taking shape on a tight October timetable. Jio Platforms, the digital services arm of Reliance Industries, is likely to get listed by the end of this month at an enterprise valuation of $143-146 billion — above Rs 12 trillion — according to banking sources cited by PTI, with the estimated $3.8 billion issue touted as the largest IPO in the country's history.

The company has concluded its overseas roadshows and is expected to file final papers with market regulator SEBI for the initial public offering in the week starting October 12, banking and other sources who did not wish to be identified told PTI. Jio Platforms did not respond to an email seeking comment.

The roadshows — held across the US, UK, Dubai, Hong Kong and Singapore — were led by Jio Platforms Managing Director and Reliance Jio Chairman Akash Ambani and Reliance Retail Ventures Executive Director Isha Ambani. One event vendor said Jio Platforms is expected to hold its India roadshow in the week starting October 12.

Context & Background

"The pricing reflects what the overseas roadshows found: strong global investor interest — the valuation band is "based on interest received from overseas roadshows," banking sources told PTI."

Jio Platforms is the vehicle that houses Reliance's digital businesses: the Jio telecom network, its broadband and enterprise connectivity offerings, and a growing stack of digital services. The IPO has been years in the making — Jio Platforms filed its draft IPO papers in June, and SEBI issued its final observations on August 28, clearing the path for the final filings now expected in mid-October.

According to its draft prospectus, the company plans to issue up to 27 crore fresh equity shares — about 2.9 per cent of its post-issue equity base. That small proportion is itself a statement: this is a listing designed to establish a public market value for a large, already-operating digital platform, not to fund a conventional infrastructure build-out. Separately, Moneycontrol has reported that Jio Platforms is eyeing a bigger enterprise and digital-services play as its heavy capital-expenditure cycle peaks.

Reliance Industries owns around 66.4 per cent of Jio Platforms, while Meta and Google — which invested during the 2020 fundraising wave — together hold about 17.7 per cent.

Impact & Analysis

At $143-146 billion, Jio Platforms would debut as one of the most valuable listed telecom and digital-services companies in the world, and its roughly $3.8 billion issue size would dwarf India's previous record IPOs. The pricing reflects what the overseas roadshows found: strong global investor interest — the valuation band is "based on interest received from overseas roadshows," banking sources told PTI.

The deal's success or stumble will set the tone for India's equity market into year-end. A $3.8 billion anchor-and-public offer will test the depth of both foreign institutional and domestic demand; it also marks the first public offer of a Reliance consumer business and the group's first IPO since 2008, making it a generational event for the Indian market.

The timeline is compressed by the calendar. Sources expect the anchor round before Dussehra, the issue opening after the festival but before October 23, and the listing itself by month-end — a schedule that leaves little room for slippage.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, the listing arrives in a familiar currency: at $143-146 billion, Jio Platforms stands alongside global telecom and technology giants. NRIs with demat accounts linked to NRE or NRO accounts can apply for Indian IPOs on the same terms as resident investors, and this one will be the largest test yet of diaspora appetite for a flagship Indian digital asset.

What's Next

The near-term milestones are clearly marked: final SEBI filings in the week of October 12, the red herring prospectus, the India roadshow, the anchor book before Dussehra, the public offer opening before October 23, and listing by month-end. The price band and anchor participation will reveal whether the $143-146 billion enterprise valuation holds — and whether India's largest IPO can clear its own record without a hitch.
nri_angle: At $143-146 billion the valuation is legible to diaspora investors in global terms; NRIs with demat accounts can apply for Indian IPOs on the same terms as residents.
